Hirosaki City, Aomori Prefecture; Nationally Designated Historic Site; One of Japan's Top 100 Castles, No. 4
View of Mount Iwaki from the site of the castle keep (five-story keep)

The Tsugaru Plain, where Hirosaki Castle is located, is a basin surrounded on three sides by mountains: the Ou Mountains (Hakkoda mountain range) to the east, Mount Iwaki to the west, and the Shirakami Mountains to the south. Hirosaki Castle was built on the northern edge of a plateau overlooking the Iwaki River basin in the south.

The castle utilizes surrounding rivers as natural moats: the Tsuchibuchi River to the east and south, the Tsuchibuchi River's tributary, the Hashiri-zeki (also known as the Hori River), and the Ta-zeki, which flows into the Iwaki River to the north, and the Iwaki River to the west. Furthermore, water is drawn into the castle's moats to create a system of water moats.
Origins of the first lord, Tsugaru (Oura) Tamenobu
Statue of Tsugaru (Oura) Tamenobu (in front of Hirosaki Cultural Center)

The first lord of the Tsugaru domain, Oura (Tsugaru) Tamenobu, is said to have been a descendant of the Kuji or Oura families, which were branches of the Nanbu clan that held power throughout the Oshu region.

In 1571, Tamenobu, who had succeeded the Oura family, captured Ishikawa Castle, the residence of Nanbu (Ishikawa) Takanobu (a relative of Nanbu Harumasa), who was the head of the Nanbu clan. On the same day, he also captured Wadoku Castle, which was defended by a powerful general under the Nanbu clan, seizing two castles in an instant.

After Risshaku-ji Temple, I headed to Yamagata Castle.
Yamagata Castle is one of the largest castle ruins in the Tohoku region, originally built by Shiba Kaneyori and later extensively developed by Mogami Yoshiaki.

The JR tracks (Yamagata Shinkansen and Ou Main Line) run under the bridge, allowing you to view the stone walls and moats alongside the trains. It is a spot where you can enjoy the somewhat unusual combination of a castle and a Shinkansen.
Ninomaru East Otemon Gate
Equestrian Statue of Lord Mogami Yoshiaki

Mogami Yoshiaki was the older brother of Yoshihime, the mother of Date Masamune, who is known as the 'One-Eyed Dragon.' He is recognized as a hero who laid the foundation for the development of modern-day Yamagata City as the first lord of the Yamagata Domain.
